literal: Possession of perfection not leaving if desired, possession of forbearance having cherished to conduct oneself is required.
translation: If you desire your perfection of character to never leave you, you must cherish and practice forbearance.
modern: நிறைக்குணம் தம்மை விட்டு நீங்காமல் இருக்க வேண்டும் என்று ஒருவர் விரும்பினால், அவர் பொறுமையைப் போற்றிக் கடைப்பிடிக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet teaches that true perfection of character cannot endure without patience. If one desires their inner completeness and goodness to never leave them, they must actively cherish and practice forbearance. The word 'niṟaiyuṭaimai' signifies the possession of a full, unblemished moral character. By using the word 'pōṟṟi', the poet emphasizes that patience is a precious treasure that must be carefully guarded and maintained in all actions.
